protocol.matching_rule: An item matches the planted scenario containing its subject account with the largest account overlap, requiring at least min(2, item accounts) shared accounts.
protocol.flagged: NEXORA alert with band medium, high or critical; insufficient_evidence alerts are 'surfaced'.

units.scenario: Planted network. Precision, recall, F1, FPR, FNR count scenarios only.
units.alert: Review item. Alert precision = flagged items that match a suspicious scenario.
units.queue: Per-dataset analyst queue in review order; P@K and Recall@K averaged over datasets.

splits.holdout: first evaluated after the configuration was frozen

methods.label: NEXORA v2
methods.description: Full system: four structural detectors, temporal flow, peer statistics, risk-policy-v2.

methods.label: NEXORA v1
methods.description: Configuration shipped before this benchmark: funnel + chain, temporal, risk-policy-v1.

methods.label: B4 Structure + temporal
methods.description: NEXORA v2 without the peer-statistics family.

methods.label: B3 Structure only
methods.description: Every structural formation alerts, ranked by structural strength.

methods.label: B1 Monitoring rules
methods.description: Per-account fan-in/out velocity, large amount and pass-through rules.

methods.label: B0 Turnover ranking
methods.description: Accounts ranked by turnover; flags the same number of items as NEXORA v2.

methods.label: B2 PageRank
methods.description: Amount-weighted PageRank; flags the same number of items as NEXORA v2.

false_positives.notes: salary followed by remittances to relatives

perturbations.description: 5% of rows re-sent as exact duplicates
every amount perturbed by up to +/-1%
10% of accounts declared at the collection boundary
four times the unlabelled background volume

limitations: All datasets are synthetic and generated by the same team that wrote the detectors; typologies, parameter ranges and hard negatives reflect our assumptions, not observed bank data.
Scenario counts per split are small (tens per family); differences of one or two scenarios are noise.
Priority is a triage ranking, not a calibrated probability of fraud.
Latency is wall-clock time of the pure analysis pipeline on one CPU core of the benchmark machine; it excludes database I/O and is not a banking-scale throughput claim.
Legitimate hubs capped by peer counter-evidence remain alerted at medium by design; any-alert FPR therefore stays high while high-band FPR measures the prioritisation effect.
